FLEX · Oxygen and droplet burning rate

How does the reported droplet burning-rate constant change with oxygen?

151 analyzed / 274 study records · 123 excluded · Pressure band 13.961–15.431 psi

K is a droplet burning-rate constant in mm²/s. It is not the burning speed of an entire fire.

school

How to read this chart. Each dot is one reported test: oxygen on the horizontal axis, burning-rate constant K on the vertical axis. The solid line is a trend adjusted for pressure and droplet size, so it can sit away from the dots; the shaded band is the 95% interval for that trend. A line rising to the right means K was larger at higher oxygen in these tests. It is drawn only inside the oxygen range that was actually tested.

heptane · N2

0.01847

Adjusted mm²/s per O₂ percentage point 

95% model interval 0.00620–0.03075 · n=32 

Within this group, each extra percentage point of oxygen raises K by about 0.0185 mm²/s (95% interval 0.0062 to 0.0307). The interval excludes zero, so the association is distinguishable from no change. This describes these tests, not a cause.

Safety-relevant evidence: Higher K associated with higher oxygen.

methanol · N2

0.01832

Adjusted mm²/s per O₂ percentage point 

95% model interval 0.01571–0.02094 · n=41 

Within this group, each extra percentage point of oxygen raises K by about 0.0183 mm²/s (95% interval 0.0157 to 0.0209). The interval excludes zero, so the association is distinguishable from no change. This describes these tests, not a cause.

Safety-relevant evidence: Higher K associated with higher oxygen.

● dots: reported tests ━ solid line: adjusted trend ▒ shaded band: 95% interval colors: diluent gas

Evidence of burning behavior, not an ignition alarm: a positive adjusted trend means higher K is associated with higher oxygen within that group. Above/below the line is not a risk classification. The shaded band is uncertainty in the mean, not a safe operating zone.

FLEX analyzed records and provenance

These conditional associations do not establish a universal law or a fire-safety limit. Intervals assume the scatter around the trend is similar at every oxygen level, roughly bell-shaped and independent between tests; instrument calibration error, the choice of model and unreported conditions are not captured. Do not transfer near-1-atm slopes to lower pressure, other blends or lunar gravity.

FLEX at lunar-habitat conditions (not part of the fit)

FLEX tests with O₂ ≥30% and pressure ≤10.2 psi: 0. The archive's tests in that range are ACME-CFI-G gas flames; the Dashboard coverage map shows them.

For the separately labelled ≤10.5 psi comparison: 17 tests, reported pressures 10.33–10.5 psi. Counts use the source-study records and exact stored bounds, not rounded labels.

Points to the right of and above zero show measured oxygen decrease together with CO2 increase during a burn. This is atmosphere-change evidence relevant to detection research, not an ignition prediction or an exposure alarm. Zero axes indicate the sign of change only; measurement uncertainty is not quantified here.

7 pairs contain a negative measured difference and remain visible. Values are signed differences, without clamping or imputation.
